whatTheControlsDid.ALREADY_CLAIMED: Never tested on this card after the marker. Lane A did not claim while the 15:30 lease was live; it released first.
whatTheControlsDid.CARD_CLOSED: Would have refused a claim after 15:46. Nobody ran claim. status showed it. status writes nothing.
whatTheControlsDid.release: Removes claim.json and the store token. Default --reason is the string close. Does not check that the close artifact exists. The 15:32 release had no close and returned the card to the board in 284ms. The 15:48 release had a close.

releaseShape.doNot: Refuse every release that lacks a close. That strands the store token until lease expiry and forbids abandon.
shape: Split the verb. release --as close requires the close artifact and a leave_behind; missing either is REFUSED CLOSE_INCOMPLETE and the claim stays. release --as abandon requires a non-default reason and writes result=ABANDONED. The card returns to the board as claimable, not as closed. An abandon is distinguishable from untouched.
Stop defaulting --reason to close. An omitted reason is REFUSED REASON_REQUIRED.

Key release to the live claim identity (worktree+branch, or a nonce written at claim time), not only to seat. Same-seat steal is how 15:32 evicted a live worker. Steal remains possible as release --as steal --force with a reason; it is logged as STEAL so it is not indistinguishable from the holder finishing.

leaseExtend.shape: Holder-only. extend --card --seat resets expires_at to now+TTL if the caller matches the live claim identity. Logged as EXTEND. Does not transfer the claim. Mechanism 2 is not what happened this time; it remains the failure mode on a card that runs past 90 minutes. Pair it with claim-identity on release so a neighbour cannot extend a stolen lease.

bypassCostThisTime.doNotCloseTheBypass: QUEUE-INIT recorded editor/SQL/gh as honestly advisory. Closing those paths turns the queue into a dispatcher. Not recommended.
cost: Two property agents on one store-backed card from 15:30 to 15:48, then the second agent kept reading after the token moved to zoning-ingest at 15:51.

An early close at 15:46 that marked Travis/Williamson bake scans as timed out; the scans finished at 15:46:58. The second write corrected that. Operator had to open this audit to learn the writes were two lanes.
ALREADY_CLAIMED and CARD_CLOSED did no work because the second lane never re-ran claim. The expensive part of claiming (the refusal) was skipped. status was cheaper and did not bind.
bypassCostThisTime.leastResistance: Claim stays the wake verb. Make the second write a named path rather than an obligation: a closed card accepts an addendum file, not a silent overwrite of close.json. status that prints CARD_CLOSED should also print the addendum command. That is still advisory. The cost of ignoring it becomes a second artifact the planner can see, not a second claim the queue must force.

whatContradictedTheCard: The card framed the defect as ALREADY_CLAIMED or CARD_CLOSED failing to fire on a second claim. Neither refusal is in the log. The second lane used status, which is not a claim and is not logged. The queue did not permit a second concurrent claim. Nothing in the four-event log contradicted the queue's documented behaviour.
